hook: SCP-015 is a warehouse stuffed with plumbing, and the whole report fits in a handful of paragraphs. Read the containment rules slowly before you get to the description; the list of things staff may not do tells you what the pipes object to well before the text spells it out. It works best as a single image to picture rather than a plot to follow.
whyItMatters: The article has no interviews, logs or arc, only a premise and a few hard numbers, and it still lands. A building that quietly grows new pipes and tries to hook itself into the neighbors' sewers turns ordinary infrastructure into something with appetite. It is a clean example of how much a short, flat report can do when every rule in it points at the same threat.
thingsToNotice: The pipe materials are the first shock: bone, wood, pressed ash, glass, granite and human flesh, while lead, copper or PVC never turn up at all. When provoked, the bursting pipes spray their victim with things like mercury, rats, ground glass, entrails or molten iron, and they keep bursting until that person dies or backs off. The ban on repairs is the neat twist, since even trying to fix a leak counts as aggression here. The final paragraph just gives the count, 11 staff killed and 20 still missing after the thing was cut back from 11 neighboring buildings, then mentions banging and screaming heard from inside, which leaves you to work out where the missing people are.
